name: Mike Johnson
role: Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives (since 2023); Representative for Louisiana's 4th district (since 2017)
summary: Johnson is a social and fiscal conservative and evangelical Christian who describes his principles as individual freedom, limited government, rule of law, peace through strength, fiscal responsibility, free markets and human dignity. A former Alliance Defending Freedom attorney, he opposes abortion and same-sex marriage, supports religious liberty claims, border enforcement, energy production and deregulation, and has backed Israel and the Trump administration's tariffs and military actions.

universal-healthcare.rationale: He voted for the 2017 American Health Care Act to repeal the Affordable Care Act and, as Republican Study Committee chair in 2019, led a plan to replace it (as reported by Wikipedia).

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wikipedia reports he opposed the Raise the Wage Act in 2019 and 2021, calling it "job-crushing legislation".

markets-allocate-better.rationale: His issues page says the private sector "will outperform the public sector in virtually every scenario" and that government is often the greatest obstacle to prosperity.

public-ownership.rationale: Clearly implied by his statement that the private sector outperforms the public sector in virtually every scenario and that government intervention should be limited.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He voted for the 2017 tax cuts, calls for permanent tax reductions, and attacked the 2021 Democratic bill as a tax increase; no statement favours higher taxes on the wealthy.

property-fundamental.rationale: His issues page lists the ability to own property among the natural and unalienable rights that government exists to secure.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He says government intervention and regulation should be limited, and as Speaker he promoted bills to codify deregulatory executive orders and cut red tape.

cut-welfare.rationale: He criticised the 2021 Democratic bill for increasing "government dependency", and the 2025 law he shepherded cut mandatory spending by $1.6 trillion including Medicaid work requirements.

surveillance-ok.rationale: As Speaker he sponsored reauthorization of FISA Section 702 without a warrant requirement, and said classified briefings convinced him it is vital to national security.

state-harmful.rationale: He treats government as necessary: the first obligation of the federal government is the common defense, and its purpose is to secure natural rights.

limit-guns.rationale: He said "the problem is the human heart. It's not guns" and that the right of citizens to protect themselves is the Second Amendment.

empower-police-military.rationale: He says adequate investment is necessary to keep the United States the strongest military power, and as Speaker championed defense authorization bills; no police-specific statement was found.

decide-locally.rationale: His issues page endorses "federalism, decentralized authority" as a way for government to serve the people.

traditional-family.rationale: His issues page says a just government "honors marriage and family as the primary institutions of a healthy society".

same-sex-marriage.rationale: He voted against the Respect for Marriage Act in 2022 and in 2004 argued for Louisiana's marriage amendment; in 2023 he said Obergefell is the law of the land and he respects it.

abortion-legal.rationale: At the 2026 March for Life he celebrated pro-life victories and said government should not subsidize abortion providers; he has cosponsored national abortion bans.

more-religion-public.rationale: He said the founders did not mean to keep principles of faith from influencing public life: "It's exactly the opposite."

gender-social-construct.rationale: He calls gender ideology "radical" in his 2022 bill statement and speaks of "basic truth" and objective truth about what a woman is.

reduce-immigration.rationale: His office celebrated that 2025 saw the first negative net migration in 50 years and said the Biden-era "wave after wave" of illegal migrants was a crisis.

free-trade.rationale: His issues page praises free trade agreements, but as Speaker he defended the president's tariffs and moved to block votes against them; the two point in different directions.

open-borders.rationale: He calls the open border a catastrophe, says the status quo is unacceptable, and touts completing border barrier construction and enforcement.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He criticised "radical climate bureaucrats and activists" and Biden's gas export pause, and said he does not believe the climate is changing because "we drive SUVs".

central-planning.rationale: He states that government intervention should be limited and that the private sector outperforms the public sector in virtually every scenario, rejecting state-run economic management.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: He called tariffs a tool the president used "very effectively to level the playing field", said Congress should not interfere with them, and described the goal as fairer trade deals.

political-violence-never.rationale: He told the House that political violence and its glorification are "profoundly wrong" and unacceptable.

separate-church-state.rationale: He calls the separation of church and state a "misnomer", says the phrase is not in the Constitution, and has criticised it as a tool used to censor religious people.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He calls the Bible his worldview on every issue, but also said that all of his personal convictions will not become law.

military-superiority.rationale: He says America must "remain the strongest military power on earth fully prepared and capable of defeating any adversaries".

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He made Israel aid his first bill as Speaker, called Israel America's dear friend and "greatest ally in the Middle East", and said in 2025 that the land belongs to the Jewish people by right.

school-vouchers.rationale: His office highlights the new federal tax-credit scholarship programme as support for school choice, which he backed; this is a tax credit rather than a literal voucher.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: He says Congress has a duty to bring spending under control and balance the budget, and attacked Democratic multi-trillion spending bills as reckless.

force-without-un.rationale: He called the 2026 strikes on Iran and the Venezuela operation necessary, lawful and justified, with no reference to UN Security Council approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: He said that anyone wanting his view on any issue should read the Bible, calling it his worldview, and described policy in terms of Scripture.

work-for-welfare.rationale: He defended Medicaid work requirements, saying that people able to work who refuse "are defrauding the system" and that there is a "moral component" to requiring work.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He backed the House bills to remove LNG export limits, expand refining and speed energy permitting, calling for "unleashing American energy".

night-watchman-state.rationale: He says the purpose of government is to secure rights such as life, liberty and property, but he also backs public assistance, entitlement reform rather than abolition, and other functions.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He says all men are created equal and that every person should be measured only by the content of their character, and affirms human dignity.

consent-of-governed.rationale: His issues page says "legitimate government operates only by the consent of the governed".

separated-powers.rationale: He praises the Constitution's "vital separation of powers, and a necessary system of checks and balances".

religious-exemptions.rationale: He proposed the 2015 Marriage and Conscience Act in Louisiana to protect people from state penalties for religious beliefs about marriage, and litigated religious liberty cases.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: He told Israeli settlement mayors in 2025 "we stand with you" and said every corner of the land is important, rejecting the label "occupied territories".

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He argues the founders wanted to stop the state encroaching on the church, and as a lawyer fought restrictions on religion.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He states that each branch of government must adhere to the Constitution and that ours is a government of laws and not of men.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He says the Constitution "as written" provides important safeguards against government encroachment.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: He and his wife promoted Louisiana covenant marriage, which makes divorce harder than no-fault divorce, though this was an optional form of marriage (as reported by Wikipedia).

capitalism-progressive.rationale: He calls the free enterprise system "the basis and genius of the American economy" that rewards hard work and creates upward mobility.

historical-land-claim.rationale: At Ariel in 2025 he said Scripture promised the mountains of Judea and Samaria to the Jewish people and that "they belong to them by right".

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: In a 2003 op-ed he wrote that states "have many legitimate grounds to proscribe same-sex deviate sexual intercourse"; that argued states may, not that they should, and he gave no later statement.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: As Speaker he set Capitol single-sex facilities by biological sex and backed keeping biological males out of women's sports; he also cosponsored a ban on gender-affirming care for minors.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: He said God raises up those in authority and that rights derive from God, but he also holds that legitimate government rests on the consent of the governed.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He insists the United States remain the strongest military power on earth and called for adequate investment in all branches.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: He says "ours is a government of laws and not of men" and that justice must be administered equally and impartially.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: He treats biological sex as an objective fact, urging the Supreme Court to keep "biological men" out of women's sports and praising objective truth.

spiritual-nature.rationale: His issues page says every person is made in the image of God and that government should embrace the vital cultural influence of religion and morality.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: His issues page says adequate investment is necessary to maintain air, land, sea, nuclear and cyber capabilities.

voter-id.rationale: He urges the SAVE America Act requiring proof of citizenship to register and a valid photo ID to vote, calling it "common sense".

scripture-inerrant.rationale: He praised the Ark Encounter as bringing people to the truth that what the Bible tells are "actual historical events", and represented its backers in court.

close-ties-china.rationale: As Speaker he led a package of 28 bills to counter the Chinese Communist Party and has said China poses the greatest threat to global peace.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: His issues page says public assistance programs "should be reserved only for those who are truly in need".

notes: Living person: no inferred answers; unknown answers are null. Wikipedia (March 2026 text) confirms he is living and Speaker. His 2003-2004 columns on homosexuality are old and he later said he did not remember some of them; the most recent clear public position (2023 onward) is that Obergefell is the law of the land. On free trade his older issues page (free trade agreements) points one way and his 2025-26 defence of tariffs another, so that answer is 0 at low confidence. After Dobbs he said abortion policy is for the states and in 2024 said he would not push a national ban, but his own March for Life speech (2026) and cosponsorship record keep the abortion answer at -2. Legislation he only scheduled as Speaker was not treated as his position unless he argued for it. Not reachable: congress.gov (blocked), the 2004 Shreveport Times op-ed archives (archive.ph captcha), axios.com and ammoland.com (blocked); speaker.gov index pages returned 404, so his own site mikejohnson.house.gov press releases were used instead. Statements on creationism in schools, death penalty, term limits and NATO were searched and found no direct statement by him, so they stay null.
